newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran tractor firm to assemble Russian cars.
newsitem.headline: Iran tractor firm to assemble Russian cars.

text.p: Iran's Orumiyeh Tractor Manufacturing Co said on Sunday it was setting up an assembly line to produce small, two-cylinder Russian cars.
Company sales manager Ali Nabizadeh told Reuters by telephone from the plant 900 km (560 miles) west of Tehran in West Azarbaijan province that production is expected to start by March 1998.
Nabizadeh would not give the name of the Russian company or the cost of setting up the plant.

Iran's official news agency IRNA had on Friday quoted West Azarbaijan governor Ali Saadat as saying the tractor company was providing 70 percent of the investment. The rest would be raised through borrowing from local banks.
He said 35 percent of the car parts would be produced domestically in the first stage. Later, the percentage would rise to 90.
"The assembly line will be bought from the Russian federation through barter scheme in exchange for export of agricultural products and dried fruits to Russia," IRNA said.
